blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract describes patching COTS sUAS devices for military deployment (e.g. disabling 'tracking/telemetry beacon' or 'call home' features), but FMToolkit's commercial pitch is framed entirely as a cloud CI/CD verification step
blind_spots.operator_reality: Formal verification of code that will run ON a resource-constrained embedded flight controller has a completely different SWaP-C and toolchain profile than verifying code in a cloud CI pipeline for enterprise software modernization — the site never addresses running or validating the toolkit against the actual patched target hardware.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The current commercial product page is written for enterprise engineering leaders modernizing legacy codebases, not for embedded/tactical hardware targets.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We integrate directly into GitHub, CI/CD pipe[lines]

blind_spots.blind_spot: The DARPA abstract explicitly targets removing 'unwanted functionality (such as tracking or "call home" features or less secure modes of operation)' from COTS devices for military use
blind_spots.operator_reality: Modifying commercial hardware's behavior for military deployment sits squarely in export-control-adjacent territory, yet neither the SBIR abstract nor the website mentions ITAR, export control, or how the patched-artifact's classification is handled once delivered to a military user.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The abstract is written as a technical R&D pitch (reverse engineering, binary patching automation) rather than an acquisition/compliance document.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: military users want to first acquire COTS (like small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS)) products, then tailor their software and functionality toward operational needs before deployment

blind_spots.blind_spot: URSA just became a DCMA Recognized Assessor for the Blue UAS Cleared List and offers free mentoring on designing products to pass that assessment
blind_spots.operator_reality: This is the company's most differentiated, directly defense-relevant expertise (supply-chain security assessment gates), but it lives on a separate page disconnected from the FMToolkit commercialization push that a 3-5 person team is racing a 12-month DARPA EEI clock to complete — a tiny team split across two distinct value props (a commercial devtool vs. a defense assessment service) is a classic setup for neither one fully fielding before funding runs out.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The site treats Blue UAS assessment work and FMToolkit as separate initiatives with no cross-linking or shared narrative.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We are particularly interested in helping companies design their products, supply chains, and manufacturing processes to align with the assessment process as early as possible.

opener_hook: You're now a DCMA Recognized Assessor for Blue UAS — does FMToolkit's formal-verification pipeline run the same way on the embedded target you're patching as it does in a cloud CI job?
what_they_do: Formal-methods code verification toolkit (FMToolkit) for AI-generated code correctness, alongside DARPA-funded work reverse-engineering and patching COTS devices (e.g. sUAS) for military use, and DCMA Blue UAS supply-chain security assessments.
